extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of philosophy and history of science; readers learning Baconian method and scientific method principles
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative standards for natural-philosophical inquiry drawn from Bacon's Novum Organum and editorial commentary: how to conduct induction, design experiments, avoid cognitive idols, and handle definitions. Useful for assessing or producing work in history/philosophy of science and for methodological critique of empirical research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form conclusions from instances and suitable experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Omnis verior interpretatio naturae conficitur per instantias, et experimenta idonea et apposita; ubi sensus de experimento tantum, experimentum de natura et re ipsa judicat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation of nature must be built from carefully chosen instances and appropriate experiments; senses only directly apprehend experiments, and experiments are the judges of nature itself. Emphasize designed, apposite trials rather than mere casual observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissect nature by analysis before forming abstractions
rubrics_metrics.description: Melius autem est naturam secare, quam abstrahere; It is better to dissect nature by means of analysis, than to form abstract theories about her.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform minute examination and interrogation of natural facts (analysis) prior to constructing abstract general theories. Abstraction and definition should follow the inductive stage, not precede it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make definitions provisional and subordinate to induction
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions ought to follow and not precede the work of 'dissection'... if ventured before, they should be regarded as incomplete and provisional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In natural and material sciences definitions are provisional; construct them only after classifying important properties by induction, and hold them open to constant review and correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware Idola tribus (tribal idols) — universal human biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Idola, quae vocamus idola tribub: arising from human nature — man projects his own aims and ideas on the Universe; the Will and Affections warp judgments; impatience rejects difficult inquiries; superstition, arrogance, and popular opinion corrupt the intellect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and correct for innate human tendencies (projection of human aims, wishful belief, impatience, pride) that bias observation and interpretation; avoid treating seemingly ultimate ‘forms’ or laws as final explanations when they may reflect human cognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware Idola specus (cave idols) — individual and educational biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Idola specus ortum habent ex propria cujusque natura et animi et corporis; atque etiam ex educatione, et consuetudine, et fortuitis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for biases arising from an individual's temperament, upbringing, habitual practices, or specialised training; those attached to particular sciences or private contemplations may distort universals from particulars (examples: some followers of Aristotle, alchemists).

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware Idola fori (marketplace idols) — linguistic and social distortions
rubrics_metrics.description: Idola fori... which from the commerce of words and names insinuate themselves into the intellect. Words often inherit popular uses and thus mislead; words can reflect and then reflect back upon intellect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let words and conventional names dominate thought; avoid disputes that end merely in verbal quibbles. In natural inquiry, start from particular instances rather than abstract verbal definitions; when definitions are used, be aware of their limits and the need for continual rectification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate minute (particle) study with compositional (holistic) contemplation
rubrics_metrics.description: Contemplations of nature in its simplicity break and diminish the intellect; contemplations of composition and configuration stupefy and dissolve it... they should be alternated so the intellect is at once penetrating and capacious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid extremes of focusing only on minute particles or only on wholes; alternate analytical, particle-level investigation with studies of composition and arrangement to keep the intellect both discerning and integrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use instruments and corrective methods to remediate sense-deception
rubrics_metrics.description: The dullness, incompetency, and deceptions of the senses have been, to a great extent, remedied by the discovery of new instruments, by methods of corrections, and by more careful discrimination between our original perceptions and the subsequent operations of the intellect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extend and correct sensory observation via instruments and systematic methods; explicitly discriminate raw perception from intellectual inferences drawn from it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep intellectual prudence to check idols arising from excess or predominance
rubrics_metrics.description: Talis esto prudentia contemplativa in arcendis et summovendis idolis specus; generaliter pro suspecto habendum unicuique rerum naturam contemplanti quicquid intellectum suum potissimum capit et detinet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt contemplative prudence: be particularly cautious about mental tendencies that most strongly capture and hold your attention (predominance, excess of composition or division, focus on large or minute objects). Apply greater caution to preserve an even and pure intellect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer material constitution and schemes (latens schematismus) in investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Materia potius considerari debet, et ejus schematismi, et meta-schematismi, atque actus purus et lex actus sive motus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on material constitution, arrangements of particles (schematism / meta-schematismus), and the laws governing processes and results, rather than on metaphysical ‘forms’ divorced from material investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid making words and names substitute for reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Credunt enim homines, rationem suam verbis imperare. Sed fit etiam ut verba vim suam super intellectum retorqueant et reflectant; quod philosophiam et scientias reddidit sophisticas et inactivas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be suspicious of arguments that rely on verbal dominance; when disputation becomes about names rather than facts, it produces sterile sophistry. Begin, where appropriate, with clear definitions (especially in mathematics), but in natural inquiry return to particulars and experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize different intellectual temperaments (resemblance vs difference)
rubrics_metrics.description: What distinguishes minds is that some are stronger to note differences and others to note resemblances; each faculty can run into excess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate methods and thinkers with awareness of their cognitive bent: critical/logical (difference-focused) versus imaginative/synthetical (resemblance-focused). Balance and avoid excesses of either tendency in scientific work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not let admiration of antiquity or novelty govern judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Reperiuntur ingenia alia in admirationem antiquitatis, alia in amorem et amplexum novitatis... Veritas autem non a felicitare temporis... sed a lumine naturae et experientiae, quod aeternum est, petenda est.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject deference based solely on age or novelty; seek truth in the light of nature and experiment, not in fashion or temporal favour. Guard the intellect against being swept by admiration of the old or the new.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat some general laws as ultimate for practical inquiry but avoid speculative explanations beyond them
rubrics_metrics.description: There are certain great laws of nature... to be taken for granted, and it is mere idle speculation to try and trace the course of nature beyond them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For practical scientific work, some general laws may be accepted as ultimate working principles; avoid speculative metaphysical searches that try to explain beyond empirically grounded laws when such attempts obstruct investigation.
